nodes.name: Sunlight
nodes.desc: Intense year-round sun powers the few plants that survive, but it also bakes the surface to extreme temperatures.

nodes.name: Rare rainfall
nodes.desc: Rain is scarce and unpredictable across the Sahara. A shower can briefly turn dry wadis and sand green with grasses.

nodes.name: Oasis groundwater
nodes.desc: Water close to the surface at oases and in wadis lets trees and palms grow where the surrounding desert is bare.

nodes.name: Sandy, nutrient-poor soil
nodes.desc: Sand and gravel hold little organic matter. Windblown dust is one source of nutrients.

nodes.name: Decomposers
nodes.desc: Beetles, termites and microbes break down dung, dead plants and carcasses, returning nutrients to the sand.

nodes.name: Desert grasses
nodes.desc: Tough, drought-adapted grasses grow in sparse tufts and sprout quickly after rain. Their leaves and seeds feed many desert animals.

nodes.name: Acacia trees
nodes.desc: Thorny acacias grow in wadis where moisture collects. Their leaves and pods are browsed by gazelles, addax and others.

nodes.name: Date palm
nodes.desc: The classic oasis tree. Its sugary fruit is eaten by people and wildlife, including foxes.

nodes.name: Desert locust
nodes.desc: Eats about its own weight in green plants daily. After good rains it can form huge swarms that strip vegetation.

nodes.name: Jerboas
nodes.desc: Small, long-legged hopping rodents that shelter in burrows by day and forage at night on seeds and plant matter.

nodes.name: Crowned sandgrouse
nodes.desc: A ground-dwelling desert bird that feeds mainly on seeds.

nodes.name: Dorcas gazelle
nodes.desc: A small, fast gazelle that grazes grasses and browses acacia and other shrubs, and is a staple prey of the Saharan cheetah.

nodes.name: Addax
nodes.desc: A critically endangered antelope that grazes desert grasses and browses shrubs, and can go a very long time without drinking.

nodes.name: Barbary sheep
nodes.desc: A hardy wild sheep of Saharan mountains that eats grasses and shrubs.

nodes.name: Saharan silver ant
nodes.desc: Dashes out for only minutes in midday heat to scavenge animals killed by the heat, and then returns to its nest.

nodes.name: Horned viper
nodes.desc: An ambush snake that buries itself in sand and strikes small rodents and lizards.

nodes.name: Desert monitor
nodes.desc: A large lizard that hunts small mammals, reptiles and insects across sand and gravel plains.

nodes.name: Fennec fox
nodes.desc: A small, omnivorous fox with big ears. In Algeria it eats insects, small vertebrates and date palm fruit.

nodes.name: Lanner falcon
nodes.desc: A fast falcon that hunts birds over open country.

nodes.name: Saharan cheetah
nodes.desc: A critically endangered cheetah that hunts desert antelope and gazelles and gets water from its prey.

nodes.name: Pharaoh eagle-owl
nodes.desc: A large nocturnal owl that hunts small desert mammals and has been recorded taking fennec fox pups.
